skill.title: Coordinate plane
skill.promise: You can place a point on the plane.
skill.pipAbility: Pip can land on a point.

lessons.title: Place a point

screens.prompt: A point needs two numbers. Which pair places it?

feedback.wrong_option: One number sits on a line. A point needs x and y.

screens.correctMessage: x and y together name one point.

screens.prompt: The point is 4 units right of the origin. Set x.

feedback.too_low: x counts steps to the right. Move higher.
feedback.too_high: That x is past the point. Move lower.

screens.prompt: The same point is 2 units up. Set y.

feedback.too_low: y counts steps up. Move higher.
feedback.too_high: That y is above the point. Move lower.

screens.prompt: Which way do you write those two numbers?

feedback.wrong_option: x comes first. y comes second.

screens.correctMessage: The pair is horizontal, then vertical.

screens.prompt: Drag the tip to the point at (7, 3).

feedback.wrong_direction: The point sits up and to the right.
feedback.wrong_length: The direction is right. Match the distance to (7, 3).

screens.correctMessage: The tip lands on the point the pair names.

lessons.whyItMatters: A model stores a position as two numbers.

lessons.title: Read a point

screens.prompt: Drag the tip onto the marked point.

feedback.wrong_direction: The mark sits up and to the right of the tail.
feedback.wrong_length: The aim is right. Stretch or shorten to the mark.

screens.correctMessage: The tip is on the mark.

screens.prompt: What is the x of the point you reached?

feedback.too_low: Count the steps right from zero. Move higher.
feedback.too_high: That count goes past the mark. Move lower.

screens.prompt: What is the y of that point?

feedback.too_low: Count the steps up. Move higher.
feedback.too_high: That count is above the mark. Move lower.

feedback.wrong_option: Both numbers are zero, so the point sits where the axes cross.

screens.correctMessage: The origin is the crossing of the axes.

screens.prompt: Which pair is 2 right and 5 up?

feedback.wrong_option: (5, 2) is 5 right and 2 up. You want the smaller x.

screens.correctMessage: Right is the first number. Up is the second.

lessons.whyItMatters: Swapping the two numbers sends a model to the wrong place.
